# VR Counselling

> VR Counselling is the counselling practice of Valessa Rizzotto, MA, RCC, CCC, in downtown Vancouver, BC, Canada. Individual and couple counselling, in person and online, in English and Portuguese.

## About the practitioner

- Valessa Rizzotto is a Registered Clinical Counsellor (RCC) and Canadian Certified Counsellor (CCC) in British Columbia, and a licensed psychologist in Brazil.
- Master's Degree in Counselling Psychology, with specialized training in trauma, grief, couples therapy and sex therapy.
- Over 25 years of clinical experience across Canada and Brazil, as stated on the website.
- Member of the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors (BCACC): https://bcacc.ca/counsellors/valessa-rizzotto/
- Psychology Today profile: https://www.psychologytoday.com/ca/therapists/valessa-rizzotto-north-vancouver-bc/1222510

## Languages

English and Portuguese. Portuguese pages are under https://www.vr-counselling.ca/pt/

## Services and formats

- Individual counselling (50 minutes)
- Couple counselling (50 minutes)
- Online counselling, available to clients across British Columbia
- In-person sessions at the Vancouver office
- Free 20 minute consultation before the first full session

## Specialties

Anxiety and stress, depression, trauma, grief and loss, relationship issues, self-esteem, body image, life transitions, immigration adjustment, perfectionism, work-life balance, parenting, separation and divorce, sex therapy.

Approach: attachment therapy, psychodynamic therapy, emotionally focused therapy, mindfulness, neuropsychoanalysis.

## Articles

- [Why does my mind race at night?](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/nighttime-anxiety/): Why does your mind feel busiest when the house goes quiet? A counsellor looks at racing thoughts at night.
- [When anxiety looks like having it together](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/high-functioning-anxiety/): High-functioning anxiety can hide behind competence and a full schedule. A counsellor explains what it can look like.
- [The difference between worry and anxiety, and why it matters](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/worry-vs-anxiety/): Worry and anxiety feel alike but are different experiences. Learn the distinction and why it matters in therapy.
- [Understanding attachment patterns in relationships](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/attachment-patterns/): Why we repeat the same patterns in relationships, and how early attachment experiences shape the way we connect.
- [The exhaustion of always being the strong one](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/always-strong-one/): Being the strong one can be exhausting and lonely. A counsellor reflects on how this role forms and what therapy can offer.
- [You can be surrounded by people and still feel profoundly alone](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/loneliness/): You can feel lonely even when surrounded by people. A reflection on the loneliness of not feeling truly known.
- [Why asking for help feels so hard](https://www.vr-counselling.ca/blog/asking-for-help/): Why reaching out for support feels so hard, and how exploring that difficulty can be the beginning of the work.
